ux.purpose: Show what a user changed, let them step back to any earlier state, and keep named restore points that survive the session.
ux.task: Look at what I changed a few minutes ago
ux.finding: Every row in the 'All changes' list carries a clickable timestamp labelled 'Jump to 14:32'. Clicking it does not jump or preview — it RESTORES, and the restore permanently truncates history: everything recorded after that point is deleted from the stack and the redo stack is emptied. There is no confirm, no toast, and no way back. The word 'Jump' promises navigation and the click performs an irreversible edit. The sibling surface one filter away (Milestones) confirms every restore with a banner that says 'Your current work is saved first — nothing is lost'; this path saves nothing first.
ux.evidence: ActivityView.tsx:360-393 handleTimestampClick -> composer.history.restoreEntry(entryId); aria-label/title at :536-537 read 'Jump to <time>'. HistoryManager.ts:757-775 restoreEntry clears redoStack and does undoStack.slice(0, entry.index + 1). Contrast VersionHistoryPanel.tsx:198-218 handleRestoreClick -> restoreConfirmId -> confirm band at :359-378. Searched: 'restoreEntry', 'handleTimestampClick', 'Jump to', 'confirm'.
ux.fix: Make the timestamp do what it says — preview the state, entering the same preview band the scrubber uses ('Previewing X / Nothing is written until Restore'). Restore stays a separate, confirmed action that states what it discards ('N later changes will be dropped') and, like the Milestones path, saves the current work first.

ux.task: Scrub back through my session and take the state I want
ux.finding: 'Restore this point' in the Time-Travel drawer fires straight into the same truncating restore with no confirmation, while the identical operation on a named version two clicks away shows a confirm band. A user who scrubs to explore and presses the obvious primary button loses everything after that point without being asked.
ux.evidence: TimeTravelScrubber.tsx:264-268 handleRestore -> onRestore(currentEntry.id); HistoryTab.tsx:195-201 handleScrubberRestore -> composer.history.restoreEntry. HistoryManager.ts:757-775 truncates. Confirmed path in VersionHistoryPanel.tsx:359-378. Searched: 'handleRestore', 'onRestore', 'restoreEntry', 'RESTORE_CONFIRM'.
ux.fix: One restore contract across the module: preview → confirm that names the cost → restore, with the current state auto-saved as a version first. The scrubber's own panel band already says 'Nothing is written until Restore' — make the button honour it.

ux.task: Search my saves while the scrubber is open
ux.finding: The scrubber installs a document-level keydown handler with NO guard for text fields. While it is open the History panel still renders its search input directly above. Typing a query and pressing Enter — the universal 'submit my search' gesture — is swallowed by the scrubber and executes 'Restore this point' on whatever the slider happens to be sitting on, which by default is the MIDDLE of the stack. A search keystroke destroys the user's later work.
ux.evidence: TimeTravelScrubber.tsx:270-286 document keydown: 'Enter' && !shift && !ctrl -> preventDefault + handleRestore(); no activeElement/INPUT/TEXTAREA check anywhere in the effect. The search field stays mounted while showScrubber is true — HistoryTab.tsx:272-294 renders it inside the unconditional activeView === 'saves' branch, and the drawer at :378-386 is a sibling. Contrast ActivityView.tsx:268-273, which DOES guard on INPUT/TEXTAREA. Searched: 'activeElement', 'INPUT', 'TEXTAREA', 'e.key === "Enter"'.
ux.fix: Scope the scrubber's keys to the drawer (focus-trapped, since it already claims aria-modal), or at minimum guard on the focused element the way the sibling list does. Enter should never be a destructive default.

ux.task: Preview an earlier state before restoring
ux.finding: The scrub preview is not a render of the past — it is the nearest NAMED version's screenshot. A user with no named versions (the default: versions are only created by explicit save or auto-checkpoint) gets no image at all: the preview layer is set to opacity 0 and the live canvas shows through unchanged, while the drawer confidently reads 'Previewing: 14:32 — Added block'. The user is looking at the present and being told it is the past, and the button under it restores.
ux.evidence: TimeTravelScrubber.tsx:104-115 renderPreviewForIndex -> findNearestSnapshot(versions, ts)?.visualSnapshot ?? null; :237-241 'else { layer.style.opacity = "0" }'; :131-133 the label prints regardless. The docblock at :5-16 states the tradeoff. Searched: 'visualSnapshot', 'previewSrc', 'findNearestSnapshot'.
ux.fix: When there is no frame for the scrubbed point, say so in the drawer ('No preview for this point — the nearest snapshot is from 13:05') and disable Restore, or fall back to restoring into a preview mode the user can back out of.

ux.purpose: Show what a user changed, let them step back to any earlier state, and keep named restore points that survive the session.
ux.task: Move the selection on canvas while time-travel is open
ux.finding: The scrubber claims Left/Right arrows at the document level and the canvas claims the same keys for selection navigation and 1px/10px moves. Both fire: the canvas handler runs first (React root), calls preventDefault, and the scrubber's own listener has no defaultPrevented check, so one arrow press both walks the element selection AND steps the timeline. The canvas is still fully interactive because the scrubber's overlay layer is pointer-events:none and its preview layer sits at opacity 0 when it has no snapshot.
ux.evidence: TimeTravelScrubber.tsx:271-275 ArrowLeft/ArrowRight -> preventDefault + updateToIndex, registered on document with no defaultPrevented test. useCanvasKeyboard.ts:78 'if (e.defaultPrevented) return' + :280-300 arrow cases. TimeTravelScrubber.tsx:178 layer.style.pointerEvents='none'; history.css:914-926 .tt-overlay is pointer-events:none until .active. Searched: 'ArrowLeft', 'defaultPrevented', 'pointerEvents', 'nudge'.
ux.fix: Time-travel is a mode, not an overlay — while it is on, the canvas should be non-editable and its keys inert, so arrows unambiguously mean 'step the timeline'. Say so on the canvas, not only in the sidebar band.

ux.task: Undo something I did a while ago
ux.finding: Undo is capped at 100 steps and the oldest entries are silently discarded — the list simply stops going back, with no line saying where history begins or that anything was dropped. An event for exactly this announcement was declared and never wired: HISTORY_CAPACITY_WARNING has zero emitters and zero listeners.
ux.evidence: config.ts:108 HISTORY_MAX_SIZE: 100; HistoryManager.ts:626-643 trimHistory() shifts entries off the front with no emit. events.ts:133 declares HISTORY_CAPACITY_WARNING. Searched all three spellings: 'HISTORY_CAPACITY_WARNING', 'history:capacity-warning', 'capacityWarning' — the constant declaration is the only hit in src/.
ux.fix: End the list with a stated boundary ('History starts here — earlier steps were dropped') and tell the user, once, when the cap is first hit, with the door to 'Save a version' beside it. The named-version path is the durable answer and nothing points at it at the moment it becomes relevant.

ux.task: Recover when the change list fails to load
ux.finding: The 'All changes' list has a built error state — an alert, a 'Failed to load activity' title and a Retry button — that no user can ever reach: the parent never passes `error` or `onRetry`. If the underlying read fails the list falls through to the empty state and tells the user they have 'No undo history', which is the same lie the Saves list was explicitly fixed for on its own board ('Your versions are still stored. Only this list failed to load.').
ux.evidence: ActivityView.tsx:643-658 renders the error branch off props `error`/`onRetry`; HistoryTab.tsx:333-341 mounts ActivityView with composer/searchQuery/onOpenTimeTravel/onClearHistory/canClear only — grep for 'error=' and 'onRetry' in HistoryTab.tsx returns nothing. Compare the wired equivalent at VersionHistoryPanel.tsx:290-305. Searched: 'error=', 'onRetry', 'loadError'.
ux.fix: Wire the failure through, or delete the branch. A list that cannot distinguish 'nothing happened' from 'I could not read it' will tell people their work is gone.

ux.purpose: Show what a user changed, let them step back to any earlier state, and keep named restore points that survive the session.
ux.finding: 'Clear' wipes the entire undo stack. The confirm is the same button re-labelled 'Clear all' with a Cancel beside it — it never states the consequence (undo stops working for everything before this moment, and it is not recoverable). It also lives only inside the 'All changes' filter, so the control that destroys history is hidden behind a filter chip, while the list it destroys is the one feeding the change counts shown on the Milestones filter.
ux.evidence: ActivityView.tsx:334-341 handleClearClick (two-press inline confirm), :407-435 renders 'Clear' -> 'Clear all' / 'Cancel' with no explanatory copy; HistoryTab.tsx:338 onClearHistory={clear} from useHistoryState.ts:25. HistoryManager.ts:783-799 clear() empties both stacks. Searched: 'onClearHistory', 'confirmingClear', 'clear()'.
ux.fix: Either state the cost in the confirm ('Undo will stop working for the 47 steps before now. Saved versions are not affected.') or drop the control — nothing about a session's undo stack needs manual clearing, and the button's only reachable outcome is data loss.

ux.task: Find the state I want to go back to
ux.finding: Two fundamentally different things are presented as two filters of one list. 'Milestones' are named versions in persistent storage with a documented retention rule ('50 kept, named ones never prune'). 'All changes' is the in-memory undo stack — capped at 100 and gone on reload. The chips say only 'Milestones' and 'All changes', so a user reasonably reads the second as a superset of the first, saves nothing, reloads, and finds their afternoon gone.
ux.evidence: HistoryTab.tsx:38-41 FILTER_LABEL + :242-253 chip row; :343-356 milestones -> VersionHistoryPanel (persistent, useVersionHistory), :333-341 changes -> ActivityView (useHistoryState.ts:46 composer.history.getHistoryStack, in-memory). SavesChrome.tsx:161-169 prints the retention rule under BOTH filters, which reinforces the misread. Searched: 'savesFilter', 'FILTER_LABEL', 'getHistoryStack', 'maxVersions'.
ux.fix: Name them for what survives: 'Saved versions' vs 'This session'. Put the durability sentence on the session list, not only under the versions list, and offer 'Save this point as a version' from any session row.

ux.purpose: Show what a user changed, let them step back to any earlier state, and keep named restore points that survive the session.
ux.finding: The drawer declares itself a modal dialog but has no Escape. The exits are the 'Exit time-travel' button and Ctrl+Shift+T — a chord the browser owns (reopen closed tab) and which the panel's own list handler does not implement as an exit. Escape while the drawer is open is caught by the change list and only collapses an expanded row, so the reflex key does nothing visible and the user is left with a past frame over the canvas.
ux.evidence: TimeTravelScrubber.tsx:315-318 role='dialog' aria-modal='true'; :270-286 the key handler implements ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/Enter/Ctrl+Shift+T and no 'Escape' case. ActivityView.tsx:305-310 Escape only clears expandedGroupId/showAllIds/confirmingClear. HistoryTab.tsx:184-193 registers Ctrl+Shift+T as a toggle. Searched: 'Escape', 'onExit', 'aria-modal', 'Ctrl+Shift'.
ux.fix: Escape exits the mode. Pick a chord the browser does not own, and put the exit in the canvas overlay where the user's attention is, not only in a drawer under it.

ux.task: Mark a moment I might want to come back to
ux.finding: The only control that creates a named, durable restore point is a text link at the foot of the History panel's Milestones filter. It is three navigations from the canvas (open History → Saves → Milestones), has no shortcut, and nothing on the canvas, the topbar or the save flow ever suggests it — while the retention copy elsewhere in the panel promises that named versions are the ones that never prune.
ux.evidence: VersionHistoryPanel.tsx:471-482 '+ Save a version' link inside the fab-container; SavesChrome.tsx:161-169 promises 'named ones never prune'. Doors into History: SiteMenu.tsx:198-201 'Version history' and useEditorShortcuts.ts:124-128 Cmd/Ctrl+H. Searched: 'createVersion', 'Save a version', 'forceCheckpoint'.
ux.fix: Put 'Save a version' where the user forms the intent — beside Save in the topbar, and as an action on any session row ('Save this point as a version').

ux.task: Undo a CMS binding or a media delete
ux.finding: Some features deliberately change the project outside history and disable Undo until the next recorded action. The engine announces this on its own event, and nothing in the UI listens — so the only way a user learns that Undo has been switched off is to press Cmd+Z and read a toast telling them it will not work. The switch-off is silent; only the refusal speaks.
ux.evidence: HistoryManager.ts:639-646 noteUnrecordedAction -> emit(EVENTS.HISTORY_UNRECORDED); callers BaseBindingManager.ts:106,125,134 and MediaCommandLayer.ts:108. Searched all three spellings — 'HISTORY_UNRECORDED', 'history:unrecorded', 'noteUnrecordedAction' — every src/ hit is the engine or a test; the only UI listener in useHistoryFeedback.ts:254 is HISTORY_NOOP, i.e. the refusal, not the notice.
ux.fix: Reflect the state where the state lives: disable/annotate the undo control the moment history stops covering the last action, and name the action ('Binding a field isn't undoable'). Do not wait for the user to try.

ux.purpose: Show what a user changed, let them step back to any earlier state, and keep named restore points that survive the session.
ux.task: See how far the site has drifted since the client approved it
ux.finding: The 'Now — N changes since approval' band and the per-version change counts are both computed from the in-memory undo stack. That stack is capped at 100 entries and reset to a single baseline on every project load, so after a reload the band reads 0 changes on a site that has drifted for days, and the summary line beneath it ('hero copy · 2 images') empties out. A number that resets to zero on refresh is a claim about approval drift that nothing backs.
ux.evidence: SavesChrome.tsx:89-107 counts composer.history.getHistoryStack() filtered by timestamp > approvedAt; VersionHistoryPanel.tsx:273-277 versionChangeCounts(versions, historyStack). HistoryManager.ts:136-157 the PROJECT_LOADED handler resets undoStack/redoStack and records a single 'loaded' checkpoint; :626-643 trims at 100. Searched: 'getHistoryStack', 'approvedAt', 'versionChangeCounts', 'PROJECT_LOADED'.
ux.fix: Derive drift from the persisted versions (or the approved snapshot diff the Compare view already computes), not the session's undo stack. Where the count cannot be known, say 'edited since approval' rather than a number.

ux.task: Take my version history with me / move it between projects
ux.finding: The engine can export the whole version history to a file and import one back, including a clear-existing mode. No screen calls either. A user cannot back up, move or restore their saves outside the browser they made them in — and IndexedDB is where they live.
ux.evidence: VersionTimelineManager.ts:360-389 exportVersions(download)/importVersions(file, clearExisting); VersionHistoryStorage.ts:269,284 the storage halves. Searched 'exportVersions', 'importVersions', 'VERSION_EXPORTED', 'VERSION_IMPORTED' across src/ — every hit is inside engine/ or its tests; no editor/ caller.
ux.fix: Give Saves an overflow with Export / Import, with import defaulting to merge and naming the destructive option explicitly. If this is deliberately out of scope, delete the engine surface so the next audit does not re-file it.

ux.task: See the past state while scrubbing
ux.finding: The drawer's horizontal position is hardcoded to the rail width on the left and a fixed 320px on the right. The History panel it is opened FROM is 280px wide (700px expanded) and sits on top of that left edge, so roughly the first 232px of the drawer — including the start-of-range timestamp — is under the panel. The right inset assumes an inspector that is always exactly 320px and always present.
ux.evidence: history.css:928-934 .tt-drawer { left: var(--bk-space-48); right: 320px; height: 200px }. tokens.generated.css:129 --bk-size-drawer: 280px; LeftSidebar.tsx:586 widens to 700 when expanded. Searched: '.tt-drawer', '--bk-size-drawer', 'panelWidthOverride'.
ux.fix: Anchor the drawer to the canvas region the same way the preview layer already measures #editor-canvas, instead of to two frozen numbers.

ux.purpose: Show what a user changed, let them step back to any earlier state, and keep named restore points that survive the session.
ux.finding: The scrubber opens with the slider parked at the MIDDLE of the stack — an arbitrary past moment — rather than at 'now'. Combined with the unguarded Enter key (UX-I-03) and the invisible preview (UX-I-12), the default position is both meaningless and dangerous.
ux.evidence: TimeTravelScrubber.tsx:74-78 initialIndex = Math.floor(historyStack.length / 2); sliderValue seeded from it. Searched: 'initialIndex', 'currentIndex', 'sliderValue'.
